info.description: Subsurface ocean temperature reconstruction API for the North Indian Ocean
info.title: OceanScope AI API

get.description: Returns held-out float validation metrics comparing model and competitors against ARGO observations.
Returns coordinates of matched ARGO float profiles for map marker rendering.

post.description: Answers questions with data tools over the OutputStore and moves the explorer with backend-validated UI actions. Every number in the answer is checked against tool results; if one is not, the answer is replaced by the raw results (grounded=false).
post.summary: Ocean guide (Muse Spark via the Meta Model API)

get.description: Returns the committed, human-approved event list. Events with a date in the sealed test period are hidden until the owner runs the final test. Suggested depths are snapped to model depths. Contains no model numbers.
get.summary: Curated ocean events for the time machine

post.description: Takes a spoken question (mono 16-bit PCM WAV at 16 or 24 kHz, 1 MB or less) or typed text, plus the phone's location and compass heading. Finds the first ocean cell along the heading that has water at the asked depth (as GET /nearest-ocean with min_depth_m), reads its profile on the latest available date, blends linearly between the two model levels around the asked depth, and returns a short spoken answer. No chat model is called; the location is not stored or logged.
post.summary: Glasses ocean guide: temperature where the user is looking

get.description: Returns the pre-registered headline comparison in the Bay of Bengal 50-300m with float-bootstrap CIs.
Returns 200 OK and active run_id when data is loaded, 503 otherwise.
Returns 2D grid slice for a given date, depth, and field (pred, glorys, error).
Returns active run metadata, coordinate ranges, depths, color scales, scientific caveats, and chat assistant configuration.
Returns precomputed evaluation metrics grouped by depth, season, or region.

With a compass bearing, returns the first valid ocean cell at least 5 km away along that bearing, up to max_km; without one, the nearest such cell. Uses coverage on the latest available date. With min_depth_m, only cells with a predicted value at that depth count. The location is not stored or logged.

parameters.description: Only cells with a predicted value at this depth (water at least this deep); must not be deeper than the deepest model level
parameters.name: min_depth_m

schema.description: Only cells with a predicted value at this depth (water at least this deep); must not be deeper than the deepest model level
schema.title: Min Depth M

get.summary: First ocean cell in view from the user's location (beach mode)

post.description: Makes an artistic postcard of the current view. The image prompt comes only from a fixed template filled with region names, wording computed from the model grid and the curated event title; no user text. Identical requests are served from a cache. The caption numbers come from the model outputs and are never drawn into the image.

get.description: Serves a postcard made by POST /postcard. Names are content hashes.
Returns 15-depth vertical temperature profile for a given lat, lon, and date.
get.summary: Vertical temperature profile at a point

get.description: Computes area-weighted (cos(lat)) mean, min, max, std over a sub-region or bbox.
Returns vertical slice through all 15 depths along one grid row or column.

post.description: Selects the area around a tapped point on our own rendered grid. Statistics are area-weighted over the selected ocean cells, with the same code as /region-summary. `method` says whether SAM or the similar-temperature fallback made the selection.
post.summary: Lasso a region from a tapped point (SAM 3.1, threshold fallback)

get.description: Returns daily time series for up to 366 days at a specific grid cell and depth.
get.summary: Time series of temperature at a point and depth

post.description: Transcribes one short clip (30 s or less, 1 MB or less; mono 16-bit PCM WAV at 16 or 24 kHz, which the browser converts its recording to). The audio is forwarded and discarded in memory; the browser shows the text so the user can edit it before it is sent to /chat.
